questions.question: For Q4 in PROBLEMS.md - sudo access for systemctl restart: which approach should be used for granting tunnel-manager the ability to restart cloudflared?
options: A: sudoers NOPASSWD rule for the specific systemctl restart cloudflared command
B: Use polkit rule to allow the vrooli user to manage the cloudflared unit
C: Run tunnel-manager as a systemd service with AmbientCapabilities or a drop-in override
questions.answer: Try to find a way around having to use sudo. All scenarios share the same lifecycle scripts, and we don't want to change that. See if there are other scenarios (maybe vrooli-autoheal? workspace-sandbox?) that have done sudo or other high permission types of things, and see if we can adopt any of those implementations/patterns. If elevated privileges are unavoidable, then there needs to be a way to grant access from the UX somehow. That's a hard requirement because I won't always be around my computer to do it

questions.question: For Q1 in PROBLEMS.md - remote-managed tunnel migration: should Tunnel Manager handle the local-to-remote migration automatically, document it as a manual prerequisite, or support both modes from day one?
options: A: Support both modes from day one; auto-detect current mode on startup
B: Require remote mode as a prerequisite; provide a one-time migration guide
C: Start with local mode only matching current state; add remote mode as P1
questions.answer: A: Support both modes from day one; auto-detect current mode on startup

questions.question: For Q5 in PROBLEMS.md - route manifest seeding: on first run, how should the manifest be populated from the current tunnel config?
options: A: Interactive CLI prompt showing discovered routes, ask to confirm each
B: Generate a draft routes.json file that the user reviews and manually approves
C: Fully automatic seeding from current config with no confirmation needed
questions.answer: A: Interactive CLI prompt showing discovered routes, ask to confirm each

questions.question: How should Tunnel Manager coordinate with vrooli-autoheal's existing infra-cloudflared check to prevent conflicting restart actions?
options: A: Defense-in-depth with a lock file to prevent concurrent restarts
B: Autoheal disables its cloudflared check when Tunnel Manager is detected as running
C: Autoheal check becomes report-only when Tunnel Manager is active; resumes recovery only if Tunnel Manager is down
questions.answer: A: Defense-in-depth with a lock file to prevent concurrent restarts

questions.question: What Cloudflare API token permission scope should be used for remote mode, and where should the token be stored?
options: A: Environment variable with Account:Cloudflare Tunnel:Edit and Zone:DNS:Read scopes
B: Encrypted config file managed by Tunnel Manager with the same scopes
C: Defer to Vrooli secrets management if it exists, or environment variable as fallback

questions.question: What is the target monitoring interval and acceptable latency for failure detection? The architecture doc defaults to 60s - is this acceptable for production?
options: A: 60s default - conservative, low overhead, approx 3 min detection time
B: 30s default - balanced, approx 1.5 min detection time
C: Configurable per-route with 30s default for critical routes and 60s for others
questions.answer: A: 60s default - conservative, low overhead, approx 3 min detection time
